recipes.name: Sweet Pepper Pasta Toss with Kale
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) package uncooked farfalle (bow tie) pasta
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook farfalle at a boil, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add bell peppers, kale, garlic, basil, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper; cook until vegetables are tender.
Toss farfalle in a large bowl with vegetable mixture; sprinkle with feta cheese to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Pepper Pasta Toss with Kale
raw_recipe.description: This easy veggie-packed pasta toss is ready in minutes. This recipe combines tender kale, vibrant sweet peppers, and crumbled feta for a creamy finish.

review.reviewBody: I give very few 5 stars, but this one deserves every star! I'd give it ten if I could! This is absolutely wonderful! I made a couple minor adjustments. I used whole wheat corkscrew pasta (couldn't find bow ties at a large supermarket!), doubled the kale and probably tripled the cayenne. Next time, I'll use even more kale. This dish will grace my dinner table weekly as long as kale is in season. Thank you for sharing this recipe!

First time my husband and I have eaten kale, we loved it! We had this as our main meal, by adding boneless, skinless chicken breast. With a cast iron griddle, I cooked the salt and peppered breast, then let them rest to simmer in juices, in some reynolds wrap. Sauted peppers, mushrooms, garlic, and one small onion. Added an entire bunch of kale, but first I removed the stem. Added cooked pasta to this, cut up breast, added those, poured in small amount of chicken broth. Last but not least topped with some fresh grated Parmesan, only because we don't care for feta. Delicious!!!

Very good recipe! I added 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts that I cut into chunks. I sauteed the chicken until it was almost done and then followed the recipe. Little squeeze of lemon at the end too. We loved it.

What a lovely colorful dish! I used what I had on hand (whole wheat penne, red, yellow & orange peppers and baby spinach. I also added a small chopped onion as well. I omitted the basil as I had none on hand. I seasoned the pepper, garlic and onion mix (I had about 2.5 cups of veggies) with red pepper flakes (maybe a 1/4 teaspoon). I added the spinach to the sauted vegetables for the last minute or so of cook time. I drained the pasta, reserving a cup of the cooking water. Dumped the drained pasta into the saute pan with the veggies, (wished I had used more than 1C of spinach!), added about a 1/4 C of the reserved pasta water along with about 3/4 C of crumbled feta. I served the pasta over a couple of handfuls of raw baby spinach. And topped with just a bit more feta. YUM! This will make my regular dinner rotation! I was very full and since I am only cooking for 1, there were about 3 cups of leftovers. I think it would be delightful served cold as well-maybe with a bit of sour cream added for moisture and more flavor. I am eager to try it with kale as well since kale is so healthy. I may make a special trip to acquire some kale from the farmer's market. Since I always have feta, tri-color peppers and baby spinach on hand (from Costco; this gives me a great, easy and satisying meal to make from those ingredients with leftovers to take for lunch or the next day. I generally make this recipie on my "meatless Monday" menu, though I think it would be good with some leftover

This has a good taste but was a little "dry" as there is not real sauce. Increased the amount of kale to four cups and next time will add even more. Next time I will decrease the amount of pasta by 1/2. I will also make a few changes to the directions. Will saute the peppers until soft before adding the kale, garlic and seasonings. After combining the pasta, vegetables and cheese will add some pasta water to create a little "sauce" and make it a little creamier.

This was pretty flavorful, but I was surprised at how dry the finished product was! I made a few changes, but nothing major. I used campanelle pasta, doubled the kale to two cups, and upped the basil and cayenne a bit. I used a bit of extra olive oil to cook the veggies. My husband added chicken to his helping. And I did use less feta as 8 oz seemed like a crazy amount to “sprinkle on”. Next time, I would make the following changes: I would triple the kale. To make the dish less dry, I would fold in half of the feta into the prepared pasta along with 1/4 cup pasta water in order to make a light sauce. Then I would sprinkle the rest of the feta on top. Also would consider adding cherry tomatoes or mushrooms for more flavor.

This dish is so yummy and EASY:) I also added extra kale (about 4 cups) and instead of cayenne pepper added oregano. Once the kale just started to wilt I added the pasta right into the pan and just heated through. Great way to incorporate more kale into your diet.

This recipe was delicious! I also added an orange bell pepper, a pint of cherry tomatoes, about 1/2 cup of Kalamata olives, an additional pinch of basil, plus I increased the cayenne pepper by a good bit. In all, I probably used almost 2 teaspoons of cayenne. I prefer my spiciness level to be medium.

So good. Had almost every ingredient in my sparse kitchen, meant to be. Used what I had: quinoa elbows, added 2tblsp pesto, doubled the kale and cayenne, goat cheese. It's a flexible recipe. I saw someone added kalamatas, I'll do that next time.

This was such a simple and delicious dish. I added some red onion and used the small sweet peppers, they are less expensive and taste so good. i saute'd the onions, garlic and sweet peppers first then added the kale by placing it on top and drenching it with lemon. i also added fresh basil. sooooo good.

It’s fabulous! I had lots of kale so probably added 4-6 cups. I added sliced mini portobello mushrooms because I needed to use them & kalamata olives. Hubby added fresh grated Parmesan cheese, I thought the feta was enough. I’ll make this again and again, many thanks!
It was just okay. I wouldn't miss it if I never had it again.
I really enjoy this nice simple clean recipe. It’s good whether it’s warm or cold. I will probably try this again and add a few different things although I liked it as it is.

I've been making a version of this for ten years! It's a great recipe. I use spinach instead of kale, rotini or penne pasta instead of farfalle, I skip the cayenne, and instead of feta I do parmesan and mozzarella. The whole family loves it.
Very good ! I put some of the feta water in the pasta.
I used whole wheat pasta, less feta, & a bit more cayenne, and I added chicken. VERY good! Will definitely make it again.
Great flavor, and loved the feta on top. Will be making this again.
Very good. I suggest doubling the amount of vegetables.

The only reason I'm giving three stars is that you really do have to take advice from other cooks for this to be successful. I had to increase the kale to 3 cups, increase the spices a LOT. I enjoy the idea and the fact we ate kale again on purpose. But I think the recipe needs tweaking based on many reviewers
very simple and yummy recipe, perfect if you want to get away from meats for a bit.
